item.title: Illegal parking, 16th October
item.description:
This is out of control. Cars parked on double yellow all the way from Aldi traffic lights, north, up to the start of Thomas Tallis property (opposite cul-de-sac). This morning the traffic had to slow right down (10mph) to navigate the small gap between the double-yellow parked cars and the crossing point in the middle of the road. The more you do nothing about it, the more it encourages bad (illegal) parking. Yet the council appeared scared to address the issue. Or does council housing come with a perk to park anywhere on the road?
Nearest address to the pin placed on the map (from OS Places API): Kidbrooke Park Road, Kidbrooke
Report on FixMyStreet

item.title: Broadway/Albion Road, 16th October
item.description:
Hello, Could you please clarify whether this junction is officially classified as a roundabout? There appears to be some confusion among road users, with some treating the junction as a roundabout and others not. This inconsistency could lead to uncertainty and potentially unsafe driving practices. If the junction is intended to operate as a roundabout, could consideration be given to installing the appropriate signage, road markings and symbols in accordance with the Highway Code to make this clear to all road users? Alternatively, if the junction is not classified as a roundabout, could suitable signage or road markings be introduced to clearly indicate this and help ensure that all road users understand how to navigate it correctly? I would appreciate clarification on this matter and consideration of any measures necessary to improve road safety and ensure consistency in how the junction is approached. Kind regards,

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 216, Broadway, Bexley, Bexleyheath, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet

item.title: Corner Arlington road - Inverness terrace, 16th October
item.description:
Dear Camden Council Team, I am writing to report a dangerous hole on the pedestrian pavement between Inverness Street and Arlington Road in Camden. The hole has been covered with a thin wooden board without any warning signs or adequate safety measures. This presents a serious risk to pedestrians, cyclists, wheelchair users and anyone passing through the area. I was involved in a serious cycling accident at this exact location on Wednesday, 14 October 2026, at approximately 11:00 am, resulting in multiple injuries and hospital treatment. I have attached photographs showing the hazard. Please arrange for this hazard to be inspected and made safe as a matter of urgency to prevent anyone else from being injured. Please confirm receipt of this report and advise when the necessary repairs will be carried out. Kind regards, Abdel flita

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 199, Arlington Road, Chalk Farm, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
